changes.old:
Tadakamalla et~al. study predictive versus counterfactual auditing state
\citep{counterfactual}. Their released threshold-family code uses a binary
history of length $t$: predictive queries test its total count, while
counterfactual queries test every threshold after flipping one event
\citep{counterfactualcode}. The former distinguish $t+1$ counts; the latter
jointly recover all $t$ history bits for $t\ge3$. Thus task-dependent
information requirements and exact reconstruction already have a concrete
antecedent. Our hard queries instead delete public blockers and return ridge
heads on the same stored features used for curation. Our sequential contract
also specifies fresh-state equality at the remaining budget. This compares
our contract with the inspected code, not the full scope of their paper.
The advertised approximate bound cannot be compared numerically with our
expected squared head-error bound until its success event and quantifiers
are available. We claim the stated fixed-scorer, shared-feature ridge
construction, not a new general prediction--counterfactual separation.
changes.new:
Tadakamalla et~al. formalize static summaries of binary histories through
query sufficiency and partition refinement \citep{counterfactual}.
Their Theorem~8(i--ii) requires $t+1$ states for all count-threshold
predictions and $2^t$ states for all single-bit-flip threshold queries when
$t\ge3$. Their exact reconstruction argument and released implementation
\citep{counterfactualcode} are direct antecedents to task-dependent
information bounds. The counting proof of Theorem~8(iii) requires at least
$(1-\delta)2^t$ states when the \emph{entire answer tuple} is correct with
probability at least $1-\delta$ under uniform histories. This joint success
event differs from separate success probabilities for individual queries.
Our approximation criterion instead bounds expected squared ridge-head
error for each fixed input and hard deletion probe; the two bounds are
not numerically interchangeable. Our construction uses the same stored
features for curation and ridge learning, with public-blocker deletions
exposing private signs. It also specifies canonical state after cumulative
deletions at the remaining budget. These are the scoped objects of our
results; we claim no new general prediction--counterfactual separation.

changes.old:
The
counterfactual-auditing comparison uses the pinned author implementation
\citep{counterfactualcode}: its query family and exact decoder were inspected,
but the full-paper proof and approximate-success quantifiers remain
unverified. For Dominici's thesis \citep{dominici}, the author and laboratory
pages establish its pipeline-unlearning scope; they do not establish its
operator-level guarantees or experimental results. Neither full text was
obtained. These are comparisons at the stated evidence levels, not complete
paper-to-paper comparisons or evidence that either work lacks our result.
changes.new:
The full six-page counterfactual-auditing manuscript \citep{counterfactual}
was inspected, including its sufficiency framework, Theorem~8 and proof,
validation scope, and limitations. Its approximation comparison above uses
the joint answer-tuple event required by that proof; the previously inspected
implementation remains separately cited \citep{counterfactualcode}.
Dominici's thesis \citep{dominici} remains unavailable in full text. The author
and laboratory pages establish its pipeline-unlearning scope, but do not
establish its operator-level guarantees or experimental results. That
comparison remains incomplete; absence of the text does not establish
absence of a corresponding result.

scope: Related-work comparison and full-text evidence status only; no scientific results or frozen protocol changes.
